risks.description: This vulnerability is live in production today (verified against the branch that already merged to master). Every day it remains unfixed, any signed-in user -- including a client seat -- can inject fabricated correspondence onto any issue in the tenant.
risks.mitigation: Fix on its own branch through the standard plan-build-proof loop, merge to master promptly; note that master merging does not itself deploy (the pipeline's deploy job is manual-dispatch only), so a deliberate deploy step is still needed to actually close the exposure in the running production app.

risks.description: The fix touches lib/workspace.ts (a protected path: adding a case to projectScopeOf), which the operating model requires the architect to approve before implementation starts.
risks.mitigation: Present the plan for architect approval before building; the change to projectScopeOf is additive (one new switch case) and cannot affect any other action type's staffing resolution.

risks.description: Adding a staffing check to attach mode could refuse a legitimate use the product owner did not anticipate -- e.g. an engagement leader filing mail on a project they lead but hold no explicit ProjectMember row for yet (a gap the automatic-membership work, ART-20260905-010, is designed to close).
risks.mitigation: AC4 requires no regression for a correctly-staffed actor; if the fix surfaces a real legitimate case that fails, that is itself evidence for prioritising ART-20260905-010, not a reason to leave this route unauthorised.

reasons: The fix touches a protected path and needs the architect gate before implementation starts, per the operating model's own rule.
